findings.rationale: The test replaces PaymentGateway with a MagicMock, so the real charge() arithmetic and validation never execute. The test stays green even if charge() is gutted.
findings.suggestion: Instantiate the real PaymentGateway and assert on its return value / ledger; mock only true external boundaries, never the subject under test.

findings.rationale: Named test_charge_succeeds but asserts the internal call sequence on a mock; it never checks that a charge succeeded. The name lies about the contract under test.
findings.suggestion: Rename to test_charge_asserts_call_order (truthful) and replace it with a test that asserts the settled total.

findings.rationale: Only the single happy path is exercised. The amount<=0 guard, the over-limit branch, and the short-account boundary in charge() are never tested.
findings.suggestion: Add cases for amount<=0, amount>limit, and len(account)<3 asserting the ValueError each raises.

findings.rationale: Asserts gw.mock_calls equals an exact sequence — it pins the internal call order rather than the observable outcome, and breaks on any harmless refactor.
findings.suggestion: Assert the observable result (the settled total) instead of the call sequence.

findings.rationale: Illustrative low-confidence finding on a real repo test: the happy-path resolution is covered but the not-a-repo / detached-HEAD branches may be untested. Flagged for strong-model re-judge.
findings.suggestion: Confirm the error branches are exercised; add a case for a non-repo path if not.
